Subject: Post-demo: data handling milestone — action items & compliance asks

Hi Anna — thanks again for making time today. Per our demo and discovery, attaching a first-pass set of action items for the Mutual Action Plan focused on Data Handling & Compliance. I kept this narrowly scoped so we can align quickly and not block the broader MAP.

High-level objective:
- Ensure Redwood’s runtime and integration model meet MediHealth’s PHI/PII constraints and logging/audit requirements so we can scope a pilot by end of Q3.

Proposed milestone (Data Handling & Compliance) — draft:
- Milestone ID: DH-01
- Goal: Confirm data flow, retention policy, and audit logging for PHI/PII in the pilot environment.
- Owner (Redwood): Rishi Malhotra — provide SOC2 summary, architecture diagram, and proposed retention controls.
- Owner (MediHealth): Anna Lopez / Infosec — provide list of PHI data types, retention windows, and any required encryption/KMS constraints.
- Target finish: 2026-07-15 (proposal)
- Dependencies: SOC2 evidence, network diagram, list of integration endpoints and expected QPS.
- Acceptance criteria: Written confirmation from MediHealth that proposed controls satisfy PHI/PII constraints and that Redwood artifacts (diagram + SOC2 summary) received.

Asks for next 5 business days:
1) Anna — please confirm if the target finish date (2026-07-15) is acceptable and whether Infosec requires full SOC2 report or a redacted highlights doc to start.
2) MediHealth to share the canonical retention policy owner & required retention period for each PHI category (e.g., patient records, audit logs).
3) Redwood to deliver SOC2 highlights + a simplified architecture diagram and a one-page audit-log plan (what fields we log, retention, and access controls).

I attached a quick MAP draft (spreadsheet) with milestones and responsibilities. If this looks fine I’ll move DH-01 into the shared MAP and add dates in HubSpot.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan

Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling milestone — action items & compliance asks

Tessa — thanks for the clear write-up and the draft MAP. A few clarifications from Infosec and compliance: 

- PHI scope: We will be sending de‑identified patient summaries plus occasional full identifiers for care-coordination (name, DOB, MRN). For the pilot, treat PHI as present — we need encryption in transit and at rest and strict key separation.
- Retention: For patient records we have a 7 year minimum retention requirement per our legal counsel; audit logs must be retained for 5 years.
- Audit logging: We require immutable audit trails for every model call that touches PHI fields — timestamp, caller id, endpoint, hashed input id, and redaction flag. Logs must be exportable to our SIEM (Splunk).
- SOC2: Infosec can work with a redacted SOC2 Type II summary to start; we will need the full SOC2 within the contracting process. A short bullet list of scope exclusions (if any) is helpful.
- Network: We run in a VPC with strict egress controls; if Redwood needs to provide an architecture diagram, please include whether private endpoints or an on-prem connector is required.

Next steps from our side: I’ll confirm the retention owners on Monday and share the canonical policy for audit logs. 2026-07-15 is reasonable for the milestone, provided we get the SOC2 highlights + architecture details within the next 7 business days.

Anna Lopez
Director, IT Security
MediHealth

Summary of changes / commitments (Redwood):
- Deliverables (timeline):
  * redwood-soc2-highlights.pdf — redacted SOC2 Type II summary (scope, effective dates, auditor conclusions) — ETA: 3 business days (by 2026-06-11).
  * architecture_diagram.pdf — simplified VPC/connector diagram showing private endpoint option + on‑prem connector — ETA: 5 business days (by 2026-06-15).
  * audit_log_plan.docx — one-page list of fields we log, retention knobs, and SIEM export format (JSON/CEF) — ETA: 5 business days (by 2026-06-15).
- Responsibility split (finalized):
  * Redwood (Rishi): SOC2 highlights, architecture diagram, audit log plan.
  * MediHealth (Anna / Infosec): confirmation of PHI types, retention owner, Splunk ingestion contact, and network egress rules.
- Acceptance criteria: MediHealth signs off in writing on whether the provided artifacts meet the PHI audit/logging requirements.

Quick note on PHI handling: Our hosted offering can be configured to not persist any full-text inputs by default and to emit hashed identifiers for traceability; where customers need retention we can expose retention TTLs and export hooks to allow MediHealth to retain logs in their SIEM.

Attachments included: redwood-soc2-highlights.pdf (redacted summary), MAP-data-handling-draft.xlsx (updated)
